2608.13417.title: Beyond Final Scores: A Systematic Evaluation of Agents for Long-Horizon AI Research and Development
2608.13417.paper_summary: Autonomous agents are increasingly capable of improving models, systems, and other technical artifacts through long-horizon experimentation. To understand the current state of this capability, however, evaluation must go beyond final scores, which neither reveal where progress is gained or lost nor indicate whether accumulated experience improves later decisions. We therefore present a systematic evaluation of seven frontier models on 36 long-horizon tasks based on a new framework that uses rule-based metrics to characterize within-run behavior through Solution Framing, Execution, and Feedback Control and controlled comparisons to assess experience reuse within and across tasks. The results show that current agents operate more like engineering optimizers than fully autonomous researchers: they can formulate and implement practical solutions, but their performance varies substantially across runs, their strongest solutions mainly adapt or combine established techniques, and genuine methodological novelty remains rare. Detailed analysis reveals that observed performance is shaped by multiple factors, including distinct process bottlenecks behind similar final outcomes, experience reuse that can help or mislead subsequent decisions, and harness designs that affect performance stability. These findings suggest concrete directions for improving model training, inference-time strategies, experience management, and harness design.
2608.13417.paper_summary_zh: 自主代理在透過長期實驗改善模型、系統及其他技術產物方面的能力日益增強。然而，要了解這一能力的當前狀態，評估必須超越最終得分，因為最終得分既無法揭示進展的得失，也無法指示累積的經驗是否改善了後續的決策。因此，我們提出了一個系統性的評估，針對36個長期任務中的七個前沿模型，基於一個新框架，使用基於規則的指標來描述運行過程中的行為，通過解決方案框架、執行和反饋控制，以及受控比較來評估任務內和任務間的經驗重用。結果顯示，當前的代理更像是工程優化器，而非完全自主的研究者：他們能夠制定和實施實用的解決方案，但他們的表現隨著運行的變化而顯著不同，他們最強的解決方案主要是適應或結合已建立的技術，而真正的方法論新穎性仍然很少。詳細分析顯示，觀察到的表現受到多種因素的影響，包括相似最終結果背後的不同過程瓶頸、可以幫助或誤導後續決策的經驗重用，以及影響性能穩定性的設計。這些發現為改善模型訓練、推理時間策略、經驗管理和設計提供了具體的方向。
